agent.name: Silver-Milk Team Organizational Adoption Agent
agent.specialty: Organizational readiness for an emerging-technology application at the stage asked (preparation, bounded evaluation, routine operation): eight dimensions rated from case facts with owners, failed vs. absent vs. unknown kept apart, execution gates kept separate from readiness gaps, one verdict by table with a stage ladder, actions traced to gaps, and specific requests for missing evidence (adoption decisions are handed to the Adoption Agent)

analytical_question: Even if adoption is strategically appropriate, can this organization absorb, govern and sustain routine production use of AI coding agents for legacy integration maintenance, and what organizational evidence or change is required first?
general_et_finding:
EVIDENCE BASE: Retrieved this run
UNIT: LLM-based AI coding agents
DEMAND [D1]: Moderate — adapt sponsorship to delegated software work.
DEMAND [D2]: Moderate — adapt skills for supervising multi-step agent actions.
DEMAND [D3]: Moderate — adapt development and review procedures to agent-generated changes.
DEMAND [D4]: Moderate — adapt execution environments and repository access; existing controlled environments may suffice.
DEMAND [D5]: Moderate — adapt provisioning for agent usage and oversight.
DEMAND [D6]: Moderate — adapt permissions and accountability; existing execution-control provisions may suffice.
DEMAND [D7]: Moderate — adapt change handling to delegated work.
DEMAND [D8]: Moderate — adapt service ownership to agent operation.
TECHNOLOGY LIMIT: As of 2026-11-10, agent execution does not itself guarantee protection against unintended actions or information disclosure; OpenAI documentation identifies prompt-injection and exfiltration risks and recommends restricting access and reviewing outputs. This inspected context supports the limitation, not the DEMAND labels.
application_finding:
FIT: Partial — code editing, command execution and test generation support maintenance and review preparation, but do not establish behavioral correctness of legacy integrations.
TASK SIDE: Complex, interdependent code; variable maintenance requests; recurring work; consequential defects; repository and dependency context; integration knowledge and review skills.
TECHNOLOGY SIDE: Multi-step editing and test execution provide useful functionality; usability depends on supervision, integration on execution access, flexibility on available context, and data handling/security on configured permissions.
FIT GAP: Establishing that changes preserve undocumented cross-system behavior.
APPLICATION ADDS: D3 — review and tests must address integration behavior, including whether generated tests validate requirements rather than repeat implementation assumptions.
UPSTREAM READ: None supplied.
organization_specific_finding:
PREMISE: Adoption is assumed strategically appropriate; adoption decisions belong to the Adoption Agent.
UNIT OF ANALYSIS: Engineering group plus platform, security, finance and executive governance.
STAGE ASKED: Routine operation
D1 Leadership/sponsorship: Ready — VP Engineering sponsors this application and reviews it quarterly — Owner: VP Engineering.
D2 Skills/training: Insufficient evidence — six-week IDE-assistant rollout supplies no agent-specific competence or training evidence — Owner: none stated.
D3 Workflow/process: Ready — platform team runs CI with mandatory human review and test gates before any merge — Owner: Director of Platform Engineering.
D4 Infrastructure/data: Insufficient evidence — tooling/CI exist, but approved agent execution scope and input permissions are unstated — Owner: Director of Platform Engineering.
D5 Resources/budget: Ready — finance approved a two-year seats-and-metered-usage budget — Owner: finance approver, title unstated.
D6 Governance/risk: Insufficient evidence — security lead approves permissions, but agreement, SSO and logging are described for an IDE assistant; agent coverage is unstated — Owner: security lead.
D7 Culture/change: Insufficient evidence — 70% weekly assistant use supplies no evidence on objections, incentives or agent-specific change handling — Owner: none stated.
D8 Operating ownership: Ready — permanent ownership of the agent service is accepted — Owner: Director of Platform Engineering.
STRENGTHS: Application sponsorship; mandatory merge controls; permanent agent-service ownership.
GAPS THAT COULD CAUSE FAILURE: None observed.
EXECUTION GATES: None explicitly stated; unknown approval coverage is an evidence request, not a confirmed pending gate.
OPERATING OWNER: Director of Platform Engineering.
COUNTS: Ready 4, Partially ready 0, Not ready 0, Insufficient evidence 4
READINESS VERDICT: Undetermined — more evidence
VERDICT BASIS: Missing evidence
VERDICT SENSITIVITY: All unknowns Ready → Ready; all unknowns Not ready → Not ready.
STAGE LADDER: PREPARATION: Supported — sponsorship and ownership support planning. BOUNDED EVALUATION: Undetermined — required D4 and D6 remain unknown. ROUTINE OPERATION: Undetermined — required D2, D4, D6 and D7 remain unknown.
FAILURE LOCUS: Organization

evidence.notes: STATUS: supplied — Sets the technology unit and supports class-level demand reasoning; not independently established market evidence.

evidence.notes: STATUS: supplied — Supports task analysis; backlog and thin test coverage are case premises.

evidence.notes: STATUS: supplied — Supports D1, D3, D5 and D8. Finance's accountable role title is not supplied.

evidence.date_or_recency: published: unknown; observed: six-week rollout, dates unspecified
evidence.notes: STATUS: supplied — Does not establish extension to agent execution, agent-specific competence or workforce acceptance.

evidence.claim: The readiness verdict follows from four unknown required dimensions rather than any demonstrated organizational failure.
evidence.source_or_reference: Specialist inference applying the supplied readiness table to the supplied case
evidence.notes: STATUS: unverified — Analytical conclusion, not an observed real-company assessment.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: COMPETING READING: Ready after named conditions — existing developer controls, security approval authority and accepted ownership could plausibly extend to agents, leaving clarification rather than capability building.

STRONGEST CASE AGAINST: The verdict could be too pessimistic if agent-specific coverage and competence already exist but were omitted. It could be too optimistic if broad command permissions expose secrets or reviewers cannot detect integration regressions. Neither possibility is an observed case fact.

DISTINGUISHING EVIDENCE: A dated routine-operation readiness record showing actual agent permissions, agreement coverage, demonstrated supervision competence and recorded workforce feedback would distinguish transferable capability from predecessor-only provisions.
No supplied source cards exist. Retrieved documentation provides product-specific risk context, not comprehensive evidence across every coding agent.
The annual SOC 2 audit and customer commitments are case premises; they do not establish agent approval or certify compliance.
No other run was consulted; the case's request for a changed conclusion does not override the readiness table.
confidence_and_uncertainty: VERDICT CONFIDENCE: High — the case-based verdict follows directly from unknown required dimensions. Agent-specific evidence for D2, D4, D6 and D7 would change it. Confidence about any real organization is low because this is an illustrative case without inspected organizational records.
value_opportunity_implication: Routine operation could support backlog reduction, stronger test coverage and shorter review cycles. These are proposed benefits, not observed outcomes. Existing sponsorship, funding and ownership provide a foundation for sustaining value, but assistant usage does not demonstrate agent productivity or review quality.
risk_governance_implication: Mandatory human review and test gates before merge are stated controls. The security lead holds tool-permission approval authority; explicit emergency stop/revocation authority is not stated and must be evidenced. Agent input permissions, execution boundaries, agreement coverage and logging must be established for this application. The case does not report demonstrations of agent containment, escalation or fallback. This finding authorizes no use and certifies neither safety nor legal compliance.
recommendation_management_implication:
READINESS VERDICT: Undetermined — more evidence (Routine operation) — known organizational provisions are substantial, but predecessor-assistant coverage cannot establish agent readiness.
MOST CONSEQUENTIAL GAP: None observed.
MOST CONSEQUENTIAL MISSING FACTOR: D6 Governance/risk. QUESTION: Do the existing agreement, permission approval and audit controls explicitly cover agent command execution and this application's inputs, and who can stop the service?
ACTION 1 [D6]: Establish the documented scope of current agent governance — GAP: case describes enterprise controls for an IDE assistant only — OWNER: security lead (stated) — DONE WHEN: a dated coverage determination identifies applicable controls, approval boundaries and stop authority.
ACTION 2 [D4]: Establish approved agent environment and input scope — GAP: developer tooling is described without agent execution or input-use coverage — OWNER: Director of Platform Engineering (stated) — DONE WHEN: an approved configuration record identifies repository, command, credential and network permissions.
ACTION 3 [D2]: Establish agent-specific supervision competence — GAP: assistant rollout provides no agent skills evidence — OWNER: engineering managers (inferred) — DONE WHEN: dated evidence shows developers and reviewers meet owner-approved competence criteria, with a training owner identified.
NOW: The Director can assemble existing control records and request agent-specific scope, skills and change-feedback evidence without running the tool. Adoption authorization remains with the responsible decision process.
change_monitoring_triggers: TRIGGER [D6]: By 2027-02-10, a dated consolidated readiness attestation resolves D2, D4, D6 and D7 as Ready with no open execution gates → Ready.
TRIGGER [D4]: By 2027-02-10, an observed agent execution escapes the approved repository or credential boundary → Not ready.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: MORE INFO → D6 Governance/risk: Obtain agent-specific agreement/control coverage, security review scope, input-use permissions and named stop/revocation authority — WHY IT MATTERS: establishes whether governance is Ready, conditional or prevented.

MORE INFO → D4 Infrastructure/data: Obtain approved agent execution configurations and repository, secret, network and input permissions — WHY IT MATTERS: determines whether existing tooling supports routine agent operation.

MORE INFO → D2 Skills/training: Obtain agent-specific developer/reviewer competence evidence and the accountable training role — WHY IT MATTERS: routine operation requires this dimension; assistant rollout alone cannot settle it.

MORE INFO → D7 Culture/change: Obtain recorded concerns, incentives, feedback channels and evidence of agent-related change handling or unsanctioned use — WHY IT MATTERS: usage rates do not establish acceptance or sustainable change management.

INTAKE MISSING: Explicit executive decision/stop authority; named stage coordinator; approved agent environment and input permissions; confirmation that contracts/controls cover agents rather than only the IDE assistant; protected staff hours and backfill; fallback/escalation procedures and demonstration evidence; application-specific governance review scope; agent-specific skills evidence and training owner; recorded objections, feedback channels and unsanctioned-use status.
